title: UGV GNSS outage on a real log: wheel odometry + IMU, innovation gate, drag detector
summary: Stdlib-only ground-vehicle loop on a real NCLT Segway session (2013-01-10, 1022 s, 1139 m, 42 MB download): consumer GPS at 1 Hz fused with MEMS strapdown INS (the 8-state EKF of gnss-ins-ekf-outage, imported), wheel speed + MEMS gyro, or wheel speed + KVH fibre-optic gyro. Measures dead-reckoning drift through injected 10/30/60/120 s outages and one real 39.6 s GNSS gap against NCLT SLAM truth, what a chi-square innovation gate does with real multipath, and detection time of an injected coherent drag (synthetic attack on real fixes) for the gate and an odometry-vs-GNSS displacement test, with false alarms on the clean log.
verified: Ran 2026-11-06 with /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 3.14.7, stdlib only (run with -I). fetch_nclt.py downloaded and sha256-verified groundtruth_2013-01-10.csv (20.7 MB) and 2013-01-10_sen.tar.gz (21.7 MB) from the NCLT S3 bucket in ~27 s; ugv_loop.py (all four reports, ~26 s) output saved in results/all-2013-01-10.txt and quoted in the README. Sensor conventions checked against truth (gyro z slope 0.994, KVH rate sign, wheel scale 1.07). 11 unittest tests pass with data, 7 pass + 4 skip without data; mutations (inert gate, zero drag) make the gate and drag tests fail. One session only; truth is NCLT SLAM which fuses the same wheel odometry; the drag is a position offset on recorded fixes, not an RF spoof. robot_localization, DRIFT and KF-GINS were not run.
group: Integrity and GNSS-loss response on a vehicle
shows: Real Segway log (NCLT): GNSS outages bridged by wheel odometry vs MEMS INS, chi-square gate on real multipath, injected drag detection with gate vs odometry displacement test
runtime: download 42 MB in ~30 s; all reports ~26 s; tests ~4 s
key_result: [Real NCLT log](README.md#results): 60 s outage drift median 57 m MEMS INS vs 3.9 m wheels + MEMS gyro vs 2.5 m wheels + FOG (120 s p95 34.5 / 16.7 m with wheels); gate rejected 16/40 multipath fixes and 0/800 good; injected 1 m/s drag caught by the odometry displacement test in 16-18 s (8/8), by the gate in 30-44 s; 0.1 m/s drag caught in at most 2 of 8 runs by either; 1 alarm per detector on the clean log, during a real 46-55 m multipath episode
